extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers / experimentalists (members of the Royal Society and practicing scientists of the 17th century)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidelines and practical criteria for designing, performing, and interpreting a range of physical and biological experiments (depth sounding, hydrometry, transfusion, gunnery, magnetism, botanical grafting) as conveyed in a 17th‑century Philosophical Transactions article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth measurement using pendulum and lead/ball
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a pendulum (ball) attached to a lead to determine depth by counting vibrations; compare ascending and descending times and use line vs. no-line trials to infer whether the ball reached the bottom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count vibrations per minute; if ball returned in fewer vibrations when let down without a line, this is a sign it did not reach the bottom. Perform multiple trials with different leads and designs (iron crooks, bowed points, nails set awry) to ensure the lead will carry the ball to the bottom and release. Be aware of currents and boat drift: currents may carry a floating ball aside, indicating differing under/upper water motions. Note and record depth, tidal state (e.g., near high-water), and any asymmetry between descending and ascending times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and adjustment of leads to ensure bottom contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Leads must be constructed and adjusted (conical figures, iron crooks, bent points) so they both carry down the ball to the bottom and then let it go when there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many leads will fail in either carrying down or releasing the ball; adjust by multiple trials until a lead reliably both reaches and releases at the bottom. When currents prevent perceiving contact, compare line and no-line trials for diagnostics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting undercurrents and their angle
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe displacement of the rising ball (or floating light objects) relative to the boat to infer motion of under parts of the water differing from surface motion; measure approximate angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note direction and distance the ball rises off to one side when boat is permitted to drift; such motion (observed angle ~40 degrees in reported trials) merits further inquiry and should be recorded with tidal context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring wind strength with a flat‑faced anemometric instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose an instrument with a flat side to the wind (flat side flush against incoming wind); the degree on the limb AB to which the wind raises that flat side shows wind force in proportion to the flat side's resistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orient the flat side right against wind; read the limb graduations (AB). Calibration is relative to the resistance of the instrument's flat side — change of flat area or shape changes the proportional response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measuring saltness with a narrow‑necked glass phial
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a glass phial with a very narrow neck: fill almost to the brim drop by drop, dry phial, weigh empty and with water, then gently evaporate the water to leave dry salt and weigh to determine salt proportion by weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dry the phial well before weighing. Add water dropwise until it can hold no more to ensure consistent volume. Evaporate gently to avoid loss of salt; compute salt mass as proportion of the water sample's weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boyle's graduated glass tube hydrometer
rubrics_metrics.description: A glass tube is balanced in common water by adding quicksilver until only the top appears; seal and graduate the tube so that when placed into different waters its sinking depth indicates differences in water gravity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust quicksilver so that only the top protrudes in reference water; seal and mark graduations accurately (diamond can be used). Use the sinking amount as a direct indicator of relative density when introduced into other waters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bucket design for drawing deep sea water without contamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a square wooden bucket with moveable bottoms/valves that remain open while the bucket descends (allowing water to pass through) and close when the bucket is drawn upward (preventing outflow), controlled by a weight and iron mechanism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design bottoms E E to be held open by resistance during descent and forced shut on ascent by water resistance, so that included water is retained and ambient water prevented from entering. Use this to sample salinity at different depths and infer stratification (top vs bottom) or presence of sweet water at depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vein-to-vein blood transfusion procedure (Dr. Edmund King)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare jugular veins in donor and recipient, insert pipes/quills, bleed recipient partly if necessary, then connect donor vein to recipient vein and allow a sustained stream of blood; monitor via palpation of emitting vein strokes corresponding to recipient vein pulses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant pipes/quills as usual in jugular veins. If recipient is faint, bleed some blood before transfusion to stimulate flow. Observe flow and confirm by feeling pulses: striking upper part of emitting vein should show corresponding strokes in recipient vein. Stop flow and close veins after transfusion, observe recipient recovery; be aware of coagulation in veins which may impede later sampling and compare arterial vs venous blood (e.g., carotid arterial blood is more vivid). Record quantities transfused and time durations of flows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting transfusion outcomes and diagnosing coagulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor flow characteristics and post‑transfusion properties: coagulation in veins can occur after flow, arterial blood differs in color and vigor from venous blood; post‑mortem inspection can reveal residual blood amounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flow slows or coagulates in the vein, open an artery (e.g., carotid) to sample arterial blood for color comparison. After death, inspect usual bleeding places to estimate retained blood. Use sensory/behavioral signs in recipients (activity, appetite) as indicators of transfusion effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative transfusion technique without ligature (punction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfusion can be performed by puncture (as in ordinary bloodletting) without ligature, according to reported improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newer reported methods (e.g., by M. Emmerez) claim to perform vein transfusion by puncture only; practitioners may attempt this technique to avoid ligatures, but should report particulars for replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re‑uniting separated tree bark — seasonal and procedural controls
rubrics_metrics.description: To reattach bark, cut three sides of a square section leaving the fourth uncut and bind closely with pack-thread; complete separations can be bound and plastered to encourage new rind formation, but success depends on season (spring succeeds; Michaelmas/winter fails).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binding and leaving a scar is effective in spring when sap is rising; covering with diachylon plaster and tight binding led to firm union in ~3 weeks. Attempting the same in autumn/winter when sap is low fails — document season and treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovering almost-withered cherries by root watering prior to reddening
rubrics_metrics.description: To save cherries that otherwise wither, bared roots and water them about a gallon each morning and evening for ~2 weeks before fruit reddens; this can restore and improve fruit, while untreated trees will have withered fruit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a hole around the tree's roots and apply regular watering twice daily in hot/dry seasons before reddening. Compare treated and untreated trees over a week's time to assess fruit retention and growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording botanical observations to infer physiological processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Track seasonal weight/leaf changes (e.g., American aloe) and leaf replacement patterns to infer internal circulation of nutritive juices and root dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record weights annually and seasonal leaf appearance/wither patterns; note that new leaves may be greener/thicker but not as large, suggesting possible return of juices from old leaves to roots. Preserve contextual storage conditions (hanging, dry cloth, temperature) when reporting mass loss or death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micrometer instrument specifications and precision claims (Gascoigne's instrument)
rubrics_metrics.description: An instrument dividing a foot into very many parts (claimed ~40,000 divisions) using two indexes (one for hundreds, one for hundreds' divisions) can mark very fine increments (smallest ~1/24 of an inch in the example) and be used to take terrestrial and celestial measures with high exactness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrument should be small and precise (pocket-watch size) with clear indexing. Using a rest devised for stability is recommended for celestial observations where motion complicates precision. Keep records of divisions per second and examples of terrestrial/planetary measurements when asserting precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for measuring planetary/stellar diameters with telescope
rubrics_metrics.description: Use telescope-based methods to measure planetary diameters and positions to the accuracy of a second where possible; employ supporting rests to mitigate swift planetary motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine micrometric division methods with stable rests to improve accuracy in celestial observations. Note limitations due to rapid motion of planets and remedy by mechanical supports and repeated measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrating thoracic duct communication anatomically (Pecquet method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert a quill into the thoracic duct, tie, and blow air into it to trace communication into subclavian or emulgent veins; compress veins and slit the cava to verify pathways and rule out interstitial passage between vein coats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform dissection on an appropriate subject (e.g., recently deceased woman after childbirth). Observe wind filling emulgent vein and escaping at opened cava; use manual compression to block branches and repeat blowing to see alternate escape routes, then cut the cava at the emulgent opening to confirm direct communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gunnery experiment: determining point‑blank range
rubrics_metrics.description: Place gun on a level platform pointing at a mark; set canvases/sheets at multiple distances aligned to visual lines to observe where the bullet passes relative to the mark; adjust gun elevation until bullet hits the mark and repeat at increasing distances to find point‑blank range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align under side of mark with under side of the gun cylinder and position intervening canvases so their undersides touch the visual line from eye to upper side of the mark. Use canvas holes and heights to determine how much higher/lower the bullet flies; adjust elevation incrementally and repeat trials as desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gunnery experiment: finding optimal powder charge for maximum range
rubrics_metrics.description: Fire at a moderate elevation (~20–25 degrees) and measure range with full ordinary charge; then systematically reduce charge by fractions (e.g., 1/8) across trials, then increase above original in increments, continuing until further increase does not extend range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record distances for each charge and use multiple trials for each setting to detect maximum effective charge (when range stops increasing). After finding right charge, explore range across different elevations to find greatest range overall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gunnery experiment: comparing guns by barrel length and bore
rubrics_metrics.description: Test a long gun with optimal charge, then progressively shorten muzzle by measured inches and retest to see effect on range; perform same methods across guns of differing bores. Repeat each experiment several times and take a medium value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat each configuration three or four times and compute a median/mean among trials to mitigate variability. When changing powder charge, use the previously determined optimal charge for fair comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magnetization experiments: touching/stroking needles and creating artificial magnets
rubrics_metrics.description: Touching needles on different hemispheres or poles of load-stones, or drawing them over the pole (without touch), gives needles a directive quality causing them to conform to the magnetic meridian; strength and retention vary with the nature and temper of the steel rather than stroke intensity or multiplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test needles with various loadstones and strokes; expect similar directional effects but different absolute strength depending on steel quality and temper. Small/faint strokes produce similar directional results to strong strokes. It is possible (claimed) to infuse a piece of steel with sufficient virtue to pick up several ounces of iron and cause a needle to conform to the magnetic meridian without using an existing load-stone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and taking central tendency of repeated trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Every experiment should be repeated multiple times (three or four suggested) in order to take a medium (central) value among them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat trials under as similar conditions as possible; record each result and report the medium/average to represent the experimental finding, reducing influence of outliers and mechanical variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mining observation protocol: water presence as an indicator of ventilation
rubrics_metrics.description: When digging deep underground, encountering water correlates with presence of wind/air; absence of water may be accompanied by poor air for breathing or lighting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If standing water exists in deep mines, drive adits to draw it off; when an adit opens and water runs, watch for violent release of enclosed air/wind that can be dangerous and dislodge rocks. Report depths and ventilation behavior to inform safety precautions.
